newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Asset swap behind big Naspers trade - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Asset swap behind big Naspers trade - dealers.

text.p: A 45 million rand share deal on Tuesday in South African printing and publishing house, Nationale Pers Ltd, was an asset swap between a local and offshore institution, stock market dealers said.
"It was a corporate finance deal...it's just someone trying to push some assets offshore," one dealer said.
By 1330 GMT Naspers was 10 cents weaker at 45 rand in volume of over 1.190 million shares, worth almost 54 million rand. Dealers said the single deal had seen 1.088 million units change hands.
Dealers said that asset swaps were becoming an almost daily occurence on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
"These things are happening every day. Most people are making use of the facility, so its no special deal," a trader said.

South African companies offshore investment activities are curbed by foreign exchange control regulations. Institutions are, however, allowed to invest up to 10 percent of each individual mutual fund abroad through "swapping" investments with an overseas concern.
On Monday a cluster of blue-chip shares saw heavy trade on the back of a possible swap worth around 140 million rand.
Shares which saw large volumes overnight, a sign of a foreign trade, included key iron and steel producer Iscor, foods group Del Monte (Delfood) and tyre manufacturer BTR Dunlop.
